newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal pay talks collapse in key region.
newsitem.headline: German metal pay talks collapse in key region.

text.p: Regional talks between the IG Metall engineering union and employers in the state of Baden-Wuertemberg aimed at securing agreement on wages and labour costs collapsed on Friday, the two sides said.
There had been hopes that a deal in the south-west state could then have been used in other regions to solve a bitter dispute over proposed cuts to sick pay and other benefits.
Dieter Hundt, chief negotiator for the Gesamtmetall metal and engineering employers federation, attacked trade union leaders for showing "no willingness for agreement".

The main sticking point is IG Metall's insistence that employers continue to pay sick pay entitlements at 100 percent of salary and not implement a new law designed to allow them to cut sick payments to 80 percent of wages.

Baden-Wuertemberg -- home to Daimler-Benz AG and its vehicle-making Mercedes-Benz unit -- was the first region to attempt to find a solution to the dispute after national talks between the two sides broke down last month.
Daimler in particular has been the focus of mass worker protests after it tried to impose the cuts in October, a decision it has later reversed.

IG Metall deputy chairman Walter Riester said there could now be a further attempt to seek a pilot agreement on wage and labour cost issues in North-Rhine Westphalia, Germany's main steel-making area.
Riester forecast that if talks collapsed there too, the regular wage round due to start in mid-January could be "really dramatic".
